decisions.rationale: Bitcoin's minimum relay fee is a node-selected policy rather than a consensus rule, and miners choose their own inclusion threshold. Because BTC is not protocol-required for validity of an ordinary transfer fee, the strict VA_GAS test is not met.
Bitcoin block production uses proof of work; BTC is not locked, delegated, or slashable to secure consensus.
Bitcoin changes require broad participant consensus; BTC ownership does not confer binding token-weighted proposal, voting, veto, or treasury rights.
Ethereum documentation states that gas fees must be paid in the native currency ETH.
Validators provide ETH as a security deposit and face rewards, penalties, and destruction of stake for slashable behavior.
Ethereum protocol governance is an off-chain social and technical coordination process; ETH ownership does not provide binding token-weighted governance rights.
BNB Chain documentation requires wallets to hold BNB for transaction gas fees.
BNB is delegated to validators to determine the active validator set, secure BSC, earn rewards, and remains subject to slashing rules.
Staked-BNB credit holders have live proposal, voting, delegation, quorum, timelock, and execution rights through BSC governance contracts.
UNI supplies governance rights; ordinary Uniswap execution fees are paid in the native gas asset of each deployment rather than UNI.

The current UNI specification documents governance delegation, voting, mint authority, and protocol-fee-linked burn but no consensus, service-security, or protocol-risk-absorption stake subject to protocol consequences. Governance delegation alone is excluded.
Delegated UNI voting power provides live proposal and voting rights over Uniswap governance.
AAVE governs and secures the application but is not the protocol-required network gas asset for ordinary Aave transactions.
AAVE Safety Module participants stake assets at protocol-defined slashing risk to cover deficits and receive active safety incentives.
AAVE, stkAAVE, and aAAVE voting power can approve binding on-chain Aave Improvement Proposals.
Arbitrum One fees are denominated and paid in ETH; ARB is not required for ordinary execution.

The finalized ARB staking design concerns governance delegation and prospective rewards, not validator security or protocol deficit absorption. Arbitrum dispute-protocol challenge bonds are denominated in ETH, so ARB does not satisfy the project's security-stake rule.
Delegated ARB voting power controls binding ArbitrumDAO proposals, upgrades, and treasury decisions.
